questions.question: What is the definition/basis of the 'lower-cost' vs 'higher-cost' operations grouping used in the AISC table, and does Group AISC reconcile to IFRS cost of production (including by-product revenue credit)?
questions.target_section: D008 Alternative performance measures (pp. 40-47); D006.2 Note 3 Segment analysis
questions.evidence_required: AISC-to-cost-of-production reconciliation table, by-product revenue figure, and definition of lower/higher-cost operation grouping for FY26 and FY25, in US$ and oz.
questions.closure_condition: Reconciliation from IFRS cost of production to AISC is shown and the lower/higher-cost grouping basis is stated; or confirmed absent from the report.

questions.question: What drove the +16.7% YoY increase in Group AISC per ounce (US$1,600 to US$1,867) despite gold sold rising 38.3% (196,927 to 272,373 oz)?
questions.target_section: D008 APM reconciliations (pp. 40-47); D006.2 Segment analysis; D003 CEO statement
questions.evidence_required: Breakdown of AISC movement by cost component (operating costs, royalties, sustaining capex, by-product credits) and by operation, FY26 vs FY25, with units and currency.
questions.closure_condition: Cost-component or operation-level bridge explains the unit-cost increase, allowing for mix/ramp-up explanations; or confirmed not disclosed.

questions.question: What are the quantified net (cash)/debt and net senior debt balances and the IFRS 9, restricted cash and financial liability adjustments excluded from them?
questions.target_section: D008 APM reconciliations (pp. 40-47); D005 statement of financial position (p. 17)
questions.evidence_required: Net debt / net senior debt reconciliation to borrowings and cash, with each adjustment quantified, at 30 June 2026 and 30 June 2025.
questions.closure_condition: Reconciliation table with quantified adjustments is provided; or confirmed absent.
